Lessons.Title: Absolute Value Functions (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: interpret absolute value as distance on a number line, write f(x)=|x| as a two-piece rule, and explain horizontal/vertical translations of V-shaped graphs with correct vertices and ranges. First-party Edulytiks adaptation based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 14, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/14/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/14/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source generalizes from the prior lesson's guesses/error data; this candidate retains that connection.

Independent first-party distance graph f(x)=|x−5|+2 gives the distance of x from target5 plus an additional fixed2-point penalty. The graph has vertex (5,2), axis of symmetry x=5, range [2,∞), and domain all real inputs. The ordinary distance function d(x)=|x−5| has vertex (5,0) and nonnegative outputs; the added2 shifts the graph vertically without changing the V slopes.

Write the same f by cases: f(x)=7−x when x≤5, and f(x)=x−3 when x≥5. At x=5, both give2, so the function is well-defined at the shared breakpoint. At x=2 output5 and at x=8 output5. The function g(x)=|x+3| instead has vertex (−3,0); adding a positive number inside absolute bars moves the vertex left.

Student activity: sketch f(x), d(x), g(x) with common axes, compare vertex/range, convert at least one to cases and critique a wrong transformation claim. Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, total 8): accurate distance interpretation, correct cases and endpoint, accurate graph/vertex, and clear explanations of translations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Distance function
KeyConcepts.Definition: |x−a| is the nonnegative distance from x to a.

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute value by cases
KeyConcepts.Definition: |u|=−u when u<0 and u when u≥0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph translation
KeyConcepts.Definition: f(x)=|x−h|+k has vertex (h,k), with V-shape slopes ±1.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Read h from subtraction inside; k from addition outside.

WorkedExamples.Title: Evaluate the translated V
WorkedExamples.Question: Calculate f(2),f(5),f(8) for f(x)=|x−5|+2.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: The symmetric inputs2 and8 are equally distant from5.
Thus vertex is (5,2) with reflection symmetry.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both sides have nonnegative distance plus2.

WorkedExamples.Title: Write cases and check boundary
WorkedExamples.Question: Represent f(x)=|x−5|+2 with separate linear expressions.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: At x4 left branch gives3, matching |4−5|+2.
WorkedExamples.Answer: f(x)=7−x for x≤5 and x−3 for x≥5.
WorkedExamples.Check: Branches agree at the shared input.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare horizontal translations
WorkedExamples.Question: Where is the vertex of g(x)=|x+3|?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: Absolute distance minimum is zero there.
Thus vertex is (−3,0), three units left of y=|x|.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Inside addition moves the zero to x=−3.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Omitting the vertical shift from the range
CommonMistakes.Correction: Add outside constant to the vertex output.

SummaryPoints: Absolute value is a distance function and has a V-shaped graph.
f(x)=|x−h|+k has vertex (h,k) and range y≥k for unit coefficient.
The same function can be expressed with two linear pieces.
Teacher evaluates graph interpretation and piecewise reasoning.
